{{Quote|Son of Xer!|Common Outer Rim exclamation|<ref name="xwh" />}}
'''Xer VIII''' was a [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] [[Noble/Legends|nobleman]], born circa [[25,200 BBY]], who became a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Chief/Legends|chieftain]] and later a [[King/Legends|King]] of [[Kingdom of Cron|Cron]], forging an [[Xim's empire|empire]] from the disparate elements of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. With the loot he had gained as a pirate providing him with the ambition and drive, Xer began claiming territories for his own, establishing the [[Kingdom of Argai]] from [[Dravione]] to [[Panna/Legends|Panna]]. This attracted the attention of the Kingdom of Cron, and its king, [[Ferece]], offered Xer all manner of titles in exchange for fealty. Xer, insulted, conquered the Cronese [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Chandaar]], and established himself as the new king.

He then initiated the [[Cronese Sweeps]], expanding his territories and establishing his new empire. His son, [[Xim/Legends|Xim]], proved to be an effective and competent leader, laying waste to various [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] and attracting an infamy that eclipsed even that of his father. When Xer had unified three of the [[Four Thrones of Cron]], he looked to push on toward [[Desevro/Legends|Desevro]], and the dominion of the [[Livien League]]. He was pushed back, however, and decided to focus on strengthening his existing holdings. In [[Time/Legends|time]], he allowed Xim to take his place as ruler. His son went on to greatly expand the territories held by his father, before disastrously [[Xim Wars|clashing]] with the [[Hutt Empire]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later.

==Biography==
===Ascension===
{{Quote|I boiled the same when my father gave my mother's love to a younger bird and I returned him the favor of my sword.|Xer VIII, from ''The Pirate Prince''|<ref name="xwpp" />}}
Xer VIII, born circa [[25,200 BBY]], was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] [[Noble/Legends|noble]] by birth.<ref name="tea" /> Hailing from [[Argai]], he became a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Chief/Legends|chieftain]]. This was not uncommon for sons of Argai&mdash;the cold and bitter [[Planet/Legends|planet]] was known for producing tough [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] and [[Merchant/Legends|traders]] who had a tendency to resort to piracy at any given point.<ref name="xwh" /> According to the play ''[[The Pirate Prince]]'', when Xer discovered that [[Xer VIII's father|his father]] was being unfaithful to [[Xer VIII's mother|his mother]], he took his [[Sword/Legends|sword]] to the man, [[Death/Legends|killing]] him.<ref name="xwpp" />

[[File:Tion_Cluster.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Xer and his fleet hid within the Ihala Spiral.]]
Xer had his [[Fleet/Legends|fleets]] explore the [[Indrexu Spiral|Ihala Spiral]], where they managed to carve out new secret routes and hiding places. The chieftain then had his fleets hide within the Spiral, from which they harassed shipping within the more backwater regions of the [[Kingdom of Cron]]. They also struck out and raided distant worlds such as [[Caluula/Legends|Caluula]] and [[Rudrig/Legends|Rudrig]]. Xer's forces utilized the "lighthouse network" of [[Hyperspace beacon/Legends|navigational beacons]] set up throughout the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] in order to move from world to world, and by tapping into the wealth of navigational data at their fingertips, were able to hide in the interstellar dark between [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] and wait for their prey. Xer's pirates littered the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|spacelanes]] with chunks of [[Water/Legends|ice]]&mdash;the collision warning systems of innocent travelers would then force them to revert to [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]], allowing the pirates to move in. Xer's men would later melt the ice with their [[Laser/Legends|lasers]].<ref name="xwh" /> The wealth and success of these raids drew more raiders to Xer and his fleet.<ref name="EG2W">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> The pirate chieftain went on to sire a son, [[Xim/Legends|Xim]],<ref name="xwh" /> who followed in his father's footsteps, and became a raider.<ref name="xwtd">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek02/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part I)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref>

In [[Time/Legends|time]], Xer grew to become incredibly wealthy from the excessive plunder he and his men had raided. As a result, he became far more ambitious and sought to claim territory for himself. He had already been hailed as the [[Lord/Legends|lord]] of Argai, and so he moved against [[Dravione]]. Taking the planet, he had carved out a pocket realm for himself, which became known as the [[Kingdom of Argai]]. An early victory also saw Xer defeat raiders from [[Algor]], a deed that was revered throughout the kingdom for [[Standard year/Legends|years]] to come. The Kingdom of Cron, however, was too involved in their own internal issues, and paid little attention to the advances of Xer. This emboldened the pirate chieftain, and he began cutting a swath through the [[Indrexu Route|Ihala Route]], overcoming the satrapies of younger Cronese nobles and weak descendants of long-dead [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]]. Over the space of ten years, Xer pushed the boundaries of the Kingdom of Argai, advancing toward [[Panna/Legends|Panna]] via [[Corlass]]. By the time the kingdom spanned from Davione to Panna, Xer had finally garnered the attention of the Cronese rulers on [[Chandaar]].<ref name="xwh" />

[[King/Legends|King]] [[Ferece]] of Cron, in response to Xer's rapid expansions, summoned the "lord of Argai" to Chandaar. There, Xer was offered a series of noble titles in exchange for an oath of fealty to Ferece and the Kingdom of Cron. Xer scorned the offer and was unimpressed by the court of Ferece and Chandaar. He vowed to return in a [[Standard month/Legends|month]] with what he deigned to be a suitable tribute for the court. Departing, he mustered a considerable fleet at Panna and launched a campaign toward Chandaar. The Lord of Argai [[Battle of Duinarbulon|engaged]] a Cronese battlefleet at [[Duinarbulon]] and smashed the opposition, allowing him to push on. [[Pasmin]], [[Soruus]], and [[Barancar]] fell to Xer's forces, leaving him free to finally move against Chandaar. His forces swept into the [[Capital/Legends|capital]], forcing King Ferece and his retinue to flee in terror. Xer was named the new King of Cron, and he made a vow to his new, cowering court that he would make the [[Star/Legends|stars]] tremble at his name.<ref name="xwh" />

===The Cronese Sweeps of the Pirate King===
{{Quote|Cron? Cron is dead?''"<br />"''Cron is ours.|Xer and Xim, in ''The Pirate Prince''|<ref name="xwpp" />}}
Xer initiated the [[Cronese Sweeps]], during which he subjugated a series of pocket kingdoms,<ref name="tea" /> including [[Nuswatta]], [[Eibon]], and Pasmin. Xer was feared throughout the Kingdom of Cron, as he set about reforming his lands as he saw fit. Anyone in his court who was dismissed as being useless was swiftly eliminated, along with their families and their followers. Any warlords perceived to be of worth, however, were dispatched to combat various rebellious Cronese worlds, as well as any independent territories on the fringes of the kingdom. In order to achieve this, Xer had his warlords capture the heirs of the rebel leaders as hostages, assuring their fealty. The warriors of Duinarbulon, in particular, served Xer with vigor. During the Sweeps, Xer's reputation came to be eclipsed by that of his teenage son, Xim, who emerged as a warlord during the campaign. Xim quickly became an infamous figure throughout the kingdom, laying waste to the [[Timber Palace of Pasmin]] and the [[High Fane of Xo]] on Nuswatta.<ref name="xwh" />

[[File:Three_Allied_Kingdoms.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Xer moved against the the Three Allied Kingdoms.]]
By the time the Cronese Sweeps had come to a conclusion, Xer had greatly expanded the Kingdom of Cron and strengthened its existing holdings. The King also now had a battle-hardened fleet at his disposal, and he looked to further expansion. From Dravione, he moved against [[Jaminere/Legends|Jaminere]], [[Cadinth]], and [[Barseg]]&mdash;the [[Three Allied Kingdoms]] that occupied the ringward flank of Xer's existing holdings. Xer's next targets were the worlds along the [[Back Spiral]]. He carved new territories through [[Caluula/Legends|Caluula]], [[Brigia/Legends|Brigia]], [[Eredenn Prime]], [[Rudrig/Legends|Rudrig]], and [[Tion]], and had opulent palaces constructed on [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]], which was also known as the Tionese Circle. Soon, there was but one power standing against Xer in the Tion Cluster&mdash;the [[Livien League]], a confederation of worlds comprising [[Livien]], [[Desevro/Legends|Desevro]], and [[Kanaver]]. He moved against the League, launching from [[Corlax 4|Corlax]] and Barseg, but the Cronese fleets suffered defeat at both [[Amarin]] and [[Lorrad]] in turn.<ref name="xwh" />

The Livien campaign had proved costly, and Xer took his errors to heart&mdash;he understood that he had overextended himself with his latest expansion efforts. Retreating from the Livien League's borders, he instead looked inward and began solidifying his existing holdings, completing the transformation of the Kingdom of Cron into a true [[Xim's empire|empire]]. To augment this, he had the network of navigational beacons extended along the Back Spiral and the [[Cadinth Run]], while establishing a bureaucracy that was both effective at commerce and warfare. At the same time, Xer made sure that it was clear his ambitions were merely deferred to his successors, and not to be ultimately denied. He reorganized his empire into three provinces, with the capitals being Chandaar, Cadinth, and Raxus Prime. Court rituals referred to [[Four Thrones of Cron]], however&mdash;those three worlds, and the still-independent Deservro.<ref name="xwh" /> Raxus Prime received Xer's favored attention, and he eventually deeded it to his concubines, as well as their retainers.<ref name="tea" />

===The son, the Despot===
{{Quote|Xer, unfurl your flags, reveal your fleet.|Queen Hylei Indrexu Cortess, in ''The Pirate Prince''.|<ref name="xwpp" />}}
[[File:Conquests_of_Xer.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Conquests of Xer]]

In [[25,130 BBY]], Xer VIII relinquished the throne to [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] Xim<ref name="xwh" /> and retired to [[Raxus Secundus|Raxus]].<ref name="EG2W" /> He was able to unify Deservo under his father's existing empire, giving way to the Xim Empire.<ref name="xwh" /> Although Xer had created an able bureaucracy, the empire was still finding it difficult to integrate new worlds into its fold&mdash;the conquest of Deservo allowed the Tionese to abandon their logographic writing system and adopt a new alphabetic standard.<ref name="tww">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref> According to ''The Pirate Prince'', Xer had sired four other sons during his reign: [[Xic]], [[Xil]], [[Xom]], and [[Xuc]], with [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Hylei Indrexu Cortess]].<ref name="xwpp" /> According to [[Direus'pei]]'s play [[Evocar (play)|''Evocar'']], Indrexu was the eighth [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] of Xer.<ref name="xwevo">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek05/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part IV: ''Evocar'')|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref> Xim, having killed King Ferece and recovered the crown of Cron, learned of this and slew his half-brothers, before killing his father, which then allowed him to declare himself Emperor.<ref name="xwpp" />

Xim used the skilled beings of the former Livien League to launch new campaigns that dwarfed the conquests of Xer and consequently earned the epithet of "the Despot." He greatly expanded the Tionese borders, and plundered some of Xer's former holdings, but eventually ran afoul of the [[Hutt Empire]].<ref name="nec" /> Xim's treatment by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] reminded him of how the Cronese nobles had scorned his father, and he used Xer's response as his inspiration, kindling the [[Xim Wars]].<ref name="xwh" /> Xim eventually died in a dungeon of the Hutt lord [[Kossak Inijic Ar'durv]].<ref name="nec" /> The Tion Cluster then had to suffer and endure invasion by the Hutts.<ref name="tea" /> The strength of the foundations that Xer built, however, ensured that the center of the Xim Empire stood for nearly a century before fragmenting.<ref name="xwh" />

Xer was later referenced in ''[[The Despotica]]'', a drama based on the life of Xim,<ref name="xwtd" /> though scholars would be undecided on which of ''The Despotica''s tales were based on actual events.<ref name="EG2W" /> A character based on Xer VIII also appeared in the play ''The Pirate Prince'', penned by [[Lisst'n]] dramatist [[Lyechusas]].<ref name="xwpp" /> Thousands of years later, the history of Xer's and Xim's reigns became less and less clear to scholars, and it became difficult for [[Historian/Legends|historians]] to distinguish just which accomplishment belonged to which Tionese warlord. By and large, Xer's efforts were obscured by his son's later accomplishments. Xer's name also went on to become part of a popular exclamation throughout the populace of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]&mdash;"Son of Xer!"<ref name="xwh" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|It pleases me, my son understands, and our family at last can be one.|Xer VIII, from ''The Pirate Prince''|<ref name="xwpp" />}}
Xer was a bloodthirsty individual and an aggressive warrior, claiming many territories during his reign.<ref name="nec" /> Although he was of noble birth, he chose to pursue the life of a pirate.<ref name="tea" /> This was not uncommon for those hailing from Argai&mdash;the world was infamous for breeding hard-nosed raiders and [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] who often resorted to piracy. He felt insulted when the Cronese King offered him titles in exchange for a vow of fealty, and apparently glowered at what he perceived to be the simpering courtesans who populated the court of Chandaar. In response to the insult, he waged a bloody campaign against the Cronese, and vowed to become an object of fear and respect once he had seized the capital.<ref name="xwh" />

His ruthless governing techniques allowed him to ascertain his reputation, as he effectively destroyed anyone under his rule whom he considered weak and useless, while implementing the talents of those he perceived to have worth. Under his rule, the Kingdom of Cron saw massive expansions, although he was infuriated by his defeats at the hands of the Livien League. He took the setbacks to heart and understood that he had overextended himself. He then chose to allow his successors to reap the future glories, while he spent the rest of his tenure as the ruler of his new Empire solidifying his holdings. Xer was also capable of respect for his fellow beings&mdash;the populace of Eibon, in particular, earned the consideration of the Pirate King.<ref name="xwh" />

==Behind the scenes==
Xer VIII was first alluded to as the father of the character Xim in ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', penned by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Kevin J. Anderson]], and published in [[2005]].<ref name="nec" /> He was later identified in [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="Complete">{{CSWECite|III|341|Xer VIII}}</ref>
